name: Gravemoss Biofoundry
sovereign_territory: The Ferment Quarter, a 14-square-kilometer wetland-industrial zone on the southern shore of Lake Erie near the ruins of Sandusky, Ohio. Characterized by vast open fermentation vats, climate-controlled mycelium towers, and perpetual low-lying bioluminescent fog.
founding_story: Founded in 2141 by former Great Lakes Environmental Remediation Authority microbiologist Dr. Sable Okonkwo, who was quietly defunded mid-project and decided to monetize her decade of proprietary bacterial strain research rather than surrender it to the Authority. She purchased a condemned wastewater treatment complex for Φ800,000 in scrip and within three years had synthesized the first commercially viable structural biofoam — a living, self-repairing building material now used in roughly 40% of new GLMZ construction. The corponation formally incorporated in 2144 after the Meridian Compact recognized its wetland holdings as sovereign. Okonkwo remains CEO and holds 34% of outstanding shares.
security_force: The Sporebloods — a 2,200-person internal security corps notorious for deploying aerosolized incapacitant compounds derived from Gravemoss's own fermentation byproducts. Their armor incorporates living mycelium panels capable of sealing punctures in real time. Outsiders find them deeply unsettling.
key_detail: Gravemoss holds 17 sovereign patents on organisms that do not exist anywhere else in the world. Three of those organisms are classified under Meridian Compact Biohazard Tier IV, meaning their unauthorized release would constitute an act of war. The corponation uses this as leverage in every major contract negotiation.
relationship_to_big_20: Not a Big 20 member. Actively resists inclusion, as Okonkwo considers the Big 20 framework a cartel designed to suppress disruptive biotechnology. Gravemoss sells to whoever pays — including corponations at war with each other — and has so far avoided serious retaliation by making itself structurally indispensable to the construction and agricultural sectors simultaneously.
full_text: Gravemoss Biofoundry is the dominant force in GLMZ's synthetic biology sector, controlling the production of living construction materials, industrial enzymes, and proprietary microbial fuel cell cultures that power roughly 9% of the megacity corridor's off-grid energy infrastructure. Its Ferment Quarter territory is visually unlike any other sovereign zone — a landscape of enormous open vats exhaling colored vapor, towers of interlocked mycelium blocks slowly growing toward optimal structural density, and canal networks where bioluminescent bacterial mats turn the water a pale jade green at night. Gravemoss workers, called Cultivators, undergo mandatory microbiome modification as a condition of employment, integrating select Gravemoss strains into their gut flora to enhance immune response to the working environment. Critics call this indentured biology. Gravemoss calls it a benefit package. The corponation's most controversial product line is the Verdance Series — living architectural panels that can be programmed to grow into specific structural configurations over a period of weeks, eliminating the need for conventional framing. Palladian Construction has been in quiet litigation with Gravemoss for three years over intellectual property boundaries, a dispute that has occasionally turned violent at the edges of both sovereign territories. Dr. Okonkwo is rarely seen in public and is rumored to have undergone extensive experimental modification herself, though Gravemoss press releases describe her as 'in excellent health and fully committed to the mission.'

glmzTerritory.description: The Ferment Quarter — 14-square-kilometer wetland-industrial zone on the southern Milwaukee lakefront, Zone 8. Experimental biotechnology research; one of the few corponation laboratories in the GLMZ that publishes research findings. Maintains formal collaboration agreements with Vellichor Institute.
glmzTerritory.grayZoneRelationship: The Ferment Quarter's edges are permeable by Zone 8 standards. Gravemoss recruits from Milwaukee Gray Zone communities — unusual enough to be noteworthy.
